analysis.title: Get paid to be patient
key_insights: Core message is not to time the turning point for duration. Yields are far higher than over most of the last two decades, so investors are paid to wait.
Focus for 2027 is high-quality carry while watching for chances to extend duration. The extra carry gives a cushion against further volatility, which the firm expects.
Balance of risks may shift from inflation to growth at some point, possibly in 2027, at which point duration should pay.
Yields could still rise. US inflation remains stubbornly above the Fed target, growth is resilient, and further rate hikes may be needed. Fiscal pressure and bond supply concerns add upward pressure.
History suggests investors underestimate the scale of a hiking cycle at its outset.
US growth has shifted toward AI and data centre capex, which is prone to sharp procyclical reversals. Borrowing costs may start to weigh on activity in 2027.
Short-dated credit is favoured as it is less sensitive to rising yields and less exposed to AI, since AI borrowing is concentrated at the long end.
Credit dispersion is rising, giving scope for active management, hedging the AI trade and avoiding weaker issuers. Spreads remain historically tight, so compensation must justify the risk.

Meta's early November 2026 bond offering, including its first euro-denominated sale, was issued at a notable discount despite strong demand. It shows investor circumspection over AI funding needs now that hyperscalers have moved beyond funding capex from free cash flow.
Prefers traditional infrastructure such as motorways and airports over data centres. These have lower leverage, longer track records and less growth sensitivity.

French sovereign weakness caused an inversion, with almost 40 per cent of French IG corporate bonds yielding less than comparable government debt at one point in October. Selective government spread exposure in France and Italy looks better than broad corporate credit, and select European banks, insurers and hybrids offer value. The firm stays cautious on Europe for 2027.

Emerging market debt offers attractive all-in yields. Latin America has high real yields and commodity exposure, and several European and African countries are cutting fiscal vulnerabilities. EM should be accessed as a strategic allocation rather than tactically.

The Middle East has been resilient through the Iran conflict, and fears of Asian supply disruption from blocked Persian Gulf shipments largely proved unfounded. Central banks have reacted prudently, limiting de-anchoring of inflation expectations.
EM technicals are supportive, with low net bond supply versus heavy developed market tech issuance.

key_data_points.metric: Share of French IG corporate bonds yielding below comparable government debt
key_data_points.anchor: almost 40 per cent of French investment-grade corporate bonds traded at lower yields than comparable government debt

tension_points.bull_case: At some point, possibly in 2027, risks shift from inflation to growth and borrowing costs weigh on activity, so duration pays and protects against a slowdown.
tension_points.bear_case: Yields can still rise on sticky inflation, resilient growth, possible further hikes, fiscal pressure and bond supply.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Borrowing costs beginning to weigh on economic activity in 2027, or a procyclical reversal in AI capex, would favour extending duration.

theme_stances.key_argument: Do not time the turning point for duration, and collect carry in short-dated high-quality credit in the meantime.
theme_stances.evidence: don't try to time the turning point for duration

theme_stances.key_argument: The potential scale of future AI-related issuance makes it prudent to hedge AI exposure by investing in other areas.
